newsitem.title: UK: Jersey says collective funds at record high.
newsitem.headline: Jersey says collective funds at record high.

text.p: Jersey collective funds rose 4.0 billion stg or 14 percent to stand at 31.9 billion stg at the end of Q3 1996, according to data from the States of Jersey Financial Services Department.
The number of Jersey funds increased to 321 from 302, the number of pools rose to 927 from 830 and a "significant number" of new funds and sub funds were established, a statement said.
The increase was due mainly to a rise in the value of open-ended funds, up to 25.4 billion stg from 21.1 billion stg, and in number to 250 from 227.
Overall 11 categories rose while seven fell, with good performance from bond and fixed interest funds.

In the same period closed-end funds declined slightly to 71 from 75 in number and to 6.5 billion stg from 6.8 billion in value. However the venture capital category more than doubled in value to stand at 1.1 billion stg from 471 million stg in Q2.
Jersey's FSD said the figures indicated "healthy performance by Jersey's fund industry and a strong vote of confidence in the Island".
Jonathan Overland of the Jersey Fund Manager's Association said sales of 2.3 billion stg and redemptions of 1.7 billion stg over the quarter produced a net inflow of 600 million stg.
Money market funds were up 154 million stg, European equity funds up 89 million stg, mixed investment funds 81 million stg and real property funds up 54 million stg.
